skeleton: boy standing, three-quarter view facing left, surfboard standing upright on his far side (viewer's right) with his far hand on its edge: root at the feet; body (wetsuit torso and shorts, pivot at the hips) with belly squash; head at the neck, face with eyes, brows, nose and mouth; armL (near, hanging) laid over the body with a faded top, armR (far, reaching to the board) behind; the board on its own bone on the root, behind the body; legL/legR at the hips under the shorts. Swapped-in poses: armL raised waving or pointing, armR free (the near arm shaded) when he lets go of the board, and for surf the board lying flat under his bent legs.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a boy with a surfboard. Draw this exact boy as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: his torso in the blue-and-orange short wetsuit, with its short sleeves and the shorts of the suit, as in image 1, without head, without arms and without legs: no bare arms, no hands, no legs below the shorts; the top of the neck, normally under the head, rounded.
2. the head: his head with the dark curly hair and his ears, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose, no mouth — keep the rosy cheeks; its bottom edge, at the chin and the neck, rounded.
3. the near arm: his bare arm on the left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of the shoulder (the part inside the short sleeve) down to the relaxed open hand, hanging as in image 1; its top the full, smooth, rounded curve of the shoulder.
4. the same near arm raised up high, bent a little at the elbow, the open hand up with its fingers spread, waving; its rounded shoulder at the bottom.
5. the same near arm held out straight, the hand pointing with its index finger; its rounded shoulder at one end.
6. the far arm: his bare arm on the right of image 1 drawn whole from the top of the shoulder to the hand, held out sideways with the hand curled as if gripping the edge of a board at shoulder height, as in image 1, without the board; its top the full rounded curve of the shoulder.
7. his left leg (on the left of image 1), drawn whole from the top of the thigh, normally hidden under the shorts, down to the bare foot, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded curve.
8. his right leg (on the right of image 1), drawn whole from the top of the thigh down to the bare foot, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded curve.
9. his two legs bent in a surfer's crouch, drawn together as one piece: feet planted wide apart, knees bent, from the tops of the thighs (normally under the shorts) down to the bare feet, seen from the front as in image 1; the tops of the thighs rounded.
10. the surfboard standing upright as in image 1: the yellow board with its red stripe, whole, without any hand on it.
11. the same surfboard lying flat, seen exactly from the side at eye level: a long, thin, slightly curved yellow shape with its red stripe along its edge, its nose turned up a little at the left end.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a boy with a surfboard; image 2 shows the same boy cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the boy's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the boy in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the boy's right eye (on the left of image 1): a big dark round eye with a white sparkle, as it is in image 1.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same eye sad: looking down, its upper lid tilted up towards the middle, a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim.
6. the same eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), a few small lashes, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer end.
7. his eyebrow as it is in image 1: a short dark arched line.
8. the same eyebrow sad: tilted up at its inner end.
9. his small nose as it is in image 1.
10. his mouth as it is in image 1: a big open grin showing his top teeth.
11. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink.
12. the mouth open in a small round 'o'.
13. the mouth in a small sad frown.
14. the mouth closed in a gentle smile: just a curved line.
15. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside, trembling.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a boy with a surfboard; image 2 shows the same boy and board cut into puppet parts. Draw more cut-out puppet parts of this exact boy and his board on one sheet, for when he lies on his board in the sea and paddles: the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in images 1 and 2, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the surfboard lying flat on the water seen from the front, its rounded nose pointing straight at the viewer: strongly foreshortened, a short wide yellow oval with the red stripe running away from us down its middle.
2. his head seen from the front, raised and looking straight at the viewer, the dark curly hair and both ears, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose, no mouth — keep the rosy cheeks; its bottom edge, at the chin, rounded.
3. his body lying face-down seen from the front (from the board's nose): the tops of his shoulders and his back in the blue-and-orange wetsuit going away from us, foreshortened, with his legs and feet lying behind on the board at the far end; without head and without arms; the shoulders rounded.
4. one bare arm seen from the front, reaching forward towards the viewer and down to paddle, bent a little, the hand cupped, from a rounded shoulder.
5. the same surfboard lying flat on the water seen from behind, its square tail nearest the viewer: strongly foreshortened, a short wide yellow oval with the red stripe running away from us.
6. his body lying face-down on the board seen from behind (from the board's tail): his legs lying together along the board nearest us with the soles of his bare feet towards the viewer, the back of the wetsuit and his shoulders further away, foreshortened; without head and without arms; the shoulders rounded.
7. the back of his head seen from behind: the dark curly hair and both ears, no face; its bottom edge, at the neck, rounded.
8. one bare arm seen from behind, reaching forward away from the viewer and down to paddle, bent a little, from a rounded shoulder.
9. his left leg (on the left of image 1) standing, drawn whole and smooth from the top of the thigh (normally under the shorts) down to the bare foot: one clean outline from thigh to ankle with only a soft hint of a knee, no crease and no pinch at the knee; its top a full rounded curve.
10. his right leg the same: standing, whole and smooth from the top of the thigh to the bare foot, one clean outline, only a soft hint of a knee; its top a full rounded curve.
11. the same leg in mid-step: the knee bent gently forward and the foot lifted behind, drawn whole and smooth from the top of the thigh to the bare foot; its top a full rounded curve.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No water, no splashes, no waves. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a boy with a surfboard; images 2 and 3 show the same boy and his yellow surfboard with its red stripe cut into puppet parts. Draw two more cut-out puppet parts of this exact boy lying on his surfboard, for when he paddles in the sea: the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in the images, the boy at the size he has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, far apart on the sheet, nothing touching:
1. the surfboard lying flat, seen from a three-quarter front view from slightly above: its pointed nose comes towards the viewer at an angle at the lower left, and its long shape runs back and away to the upper right, clearly a long surfboard (not round); the red stripe runs lengthwise along the middle of the board from nose to tail. The boy lies on it chest down, seen from the front: his shoulders at the front near the nose, his back, and his legs lying straight along the board behind him with his bare feet near the tail at the far end. WITHOUT his head and WITHOUT his arms: his shoulders rounded where they join.
2. the same surfboard lying flat, seen from behind and slightly above, as from the beach watching a surfer paddle out: its rounded tail nearest the viewer at the bottom, its long shape running away up the sheet towards the horizon, narrowing in perspective to its pointed nose at the top; the red stripe runs lengthwise along the middle from tail to nose. The boy lies on it chest down, seen from behind: his legs lying together along the board nearest us with the soles of his bare feet towards the viewer just above the tail, then his bottom in the wetsuit, his back, and his shoulders further up the board; the nose of the board shows beyond where his head will be. WITHOUT his head and WITHOUT his arms: his shoulders rounded where they join.

Every part drawn whole. No water, no splashes, no waves. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.
